review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the signatures of its main dependencies: selectedJointFiniteLaw_spatial_cutoff_bound, spatialMatrixBlock_bad_probability_of_exp_width, spatialMatrixBlockThreshold_pos and centeredFiniteProbabilityMeasure_noise_event_le. I found no justified generalisation. The two Erdos3 theorems are already stated for arbitrary finite types B, G, P, any residue moduli q, any positive widths V and any nonnegative densities D. Their error terms ηnorm and εtest are free real parameters. The complex-test variant is a corollary of the real one, not a more general statement. The final VectorPolynomial theorem is a packaged corollary of the normalization existence theorem. Its hypotheses mirror that theorem's, and its side conditions (hnX, hq-style positivity, width and Lipschitz budgets) are used by the dependencies. The matrix-specific objects (e : Fin 2 × Fin n ↪ G and Option (G ⊕ P) as the variable index) are required by spatialMatrixBlockBad and spatialMatrixBlockCutoff. I did not find a weaker condition or broader class that the proofs could use without new mathematics. I did not check every definition in the normalization theorem's hypotheses for further slack, so some uncertainty remains there.
